summary: Log in a customer with email and password
description: Authenticates an existing credentials auth identity and returns a JWT for the customer actor. Concrete instance of the core route POST /auth/{actor_type}/{auth_provider} with actor_type=customer and auth_provider=credentials. No store API key is required on /auth routes and no bearer token is needed. The request body is not validated by a zod schema: unknown fields are ignored; the credentials provider only checks that `email` and `password` are strings. Every authentication failure (missing/non-string password or email, unknown email, wrong password) returns 401 with type "unauthorized". The returned token is signed with the project's JWT secret and expires after jwtExpiresIn (default "1d"; this repository does not override it). If the auth identity has not yet been linked to a customer (registered via /auth/customer/credentials/register but POST /store/customers was never called), the call still succeeds with 200, but the token carries an empty actor_id: it is accepted by POST /store/customers but rejected with 401 by /store/customers/me. Password verification runs scrypt (N=2^15, r=8, p=1) on the libuv threadpool, so this endpoint is CPU/memory heavy compared to other store calls; an unknown email returns without running scrypt.

email.description: Email the credentials identity was registered with (the identity's entity_id). Matched exactly.

password.description: Plain-text password; verified against the stored scrypt hash.

token.description: Signed JWT (HS256 with the project's jwtSecret unless jwtOptions override it).

responses.description: Authenticated. Body carries the JWT to send as `Authorization: Bearer <token>` on /store/* calls. The token payload contains actor_id (the customer id, or "" when the identity has no customer yet), actor_type "customer", auth_identity_id, auth_provider "credentials", app_metadata and user_metadata. Expires after 1 day by default (jwtExpiresIn "1d"). The `location` (OAuth redirect) and `mfa_required` / `verification_required` variants of this route are not reachable for credentials with this repository's configuration (no MFA factors, no authVerificationsPerActor).

example.message: The actor type customer is not allowed to use the auth provider credentials

responses.description: The customer actor is not allowed to use the credentials provider (only when projectConfig.http.authMethodsPerActor.customer is configured without "credentials"; not the case in this repository, whose config sets no authMethodsPerActor for customer).

message.description: Known literals: "Invalid email or password", "Password should be a string", "Email should be a string".

responses.description: Authentication failed. Unknown email or wrong password → "Invalid email or password" (same message for both). Missing or non-string `password` → "Password should be a string" (checked first); missing or non-string `email` → "Email should be a string". Any other provider error is also returned here with its own message.
